title: Maharashtra Seamless Ltd - 500265 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Maharashtra Seamless Q2 FY27: seamless EBITDA/ton fell to INR9,220 (Q1: INR15,660), which management attributes to a notional inventory-valuation hit.
summary.overview: Management said Q2 margins were depressed by a notional Ind AS inventory-valuation adjustment, as steel billet prices fell below procurement cost on inventory held at 30 September 2026. Order book rose from INR1,700 crores (31 July) to INR2,200 crores, with execution lead time of 2 to 4 months. H1 seamless dispatches were around 200,000 tons, and management reiterated the 430,000-ton seamless FY27 target, requiring about 230,000 tons in H2. Other income was nil as treasury equity and gold/silver exposures marked down. Management also outlined a three-way demerger of the seamless business and a registered office shift to Gurgaon, with approvals expected by January-February 2027.

segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton of INR9,220 in Q2 versus INR15,660 in Q1, with management calling the drop notional. Dispatches rose about 7,000 tons QoQ. Order book is majority-weighted to upstream, export and value-added products.

segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton of INR1,830 in Q2. Dispatches rose about 9,000 tons QoQ. No ERW-specific order split was given on the call; the split is in Slide 15 of the presentation.

segments.commentary: Order book includes cylinder pipe orders of INR144 crores, which management confirmed fall in the high-margin category.

guidance_outlook: Seamless FY27 dispatch guidance of 430,000 tons retained; management said it is on track with about 230,000 tons required in H2.
Management expects margins to recover in Q3 FY27 (December quarter) as the notional inventory-valuation loss reverses on dispatch.
Execution time for current order book is 2 to 4 months for both seamless and ERW.
Telangana finishing line to be activated in FY27; no orders for the added capacity taken yet, to avoid raw-material exposure before commissioning.
Demerger approval from stock exchanges hoped for by January or February 2027. Anti-dumping duty re-imposition decision expected January 2027.

Management said the FY25 seamless EBITDA benchmark (about INR720 crores) may be approached or surpassed, but caveated that notional inventory adjustments can distort results in rapidly rising or falling steel prices.
capex_capacity: Telangana finishing line under implementation, to be activated in FY27; it extends the Telangana mill's range to 14 inch.
Further projects, including the INR350 crore hot mill upgrade (estimated to add about INR1,000 crores annual turnover), will only be timed after the Telangana finishing line is complete.
Post-demerger segmentation: Nagothane (0.5 to 20 inch, oil and gas, premium connections); Mangaon (0.5 to 6 inch, cold-drawn and drill pipe); Telangana (up to 14 inch, cylinder pipes).
demand_pricing: Order pipeline is good, with an uptick in upstream and export segments; export mix is materially better YoY, driven by higher North American rig counts. Export mix was the same in Q1 and Q2 FY27; no percentage was disclosed.
Oil and gas capex in India has begun to recover after 2 to 3 years of stagnation; management cited Indian deepwater tenders and awards reflected in the order book.

Import competition remains; management is awaiting re-imposition of anti-dumping duty, with a decision expected in January 2027. The DGTR recommended a flat $268/ton duty, but management declined to comment further as the matter is under consideration.
Steel billet prices rose sharply in Q1 FY27 and rose less in Q2, and inventory bought at higher prices was written down against lower September 2026 prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did seamless EBITDA per ton fall to INR9,220 in Q2, and what is the underlying trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is an inventory-valuation effect under Ind AS, which is notional. Inventory rose by more than INR500 crores as the order book grew, and September prices were below procurement cost. Underlying EBITDA per ton is better than Q1's INR15,660, and margins should recover once the inventory is dispatched.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 430,000-ton seamless guidance on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. About 200,000 tons were done in H1, leaving about 230,000 tons for H2. Telangana finishing line is due in FY27, and new orders for the added capacity are on hold until it is commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company demerging into three entities and moving its registered office?
qa_highlights.answer: The registered office moved to Gurgaon because most decisions are taken there. The three seamless entities are split by mill size range and product focus (Nagothane, Mangaon, Telangana). Scheme details are in public filings; approvals are expected by January or February 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Order book of INR1,709 crores at 31 July versus Q2 revenue of about INR1,300 crores: where is the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book is a 3 to 4 month backlog. Q2 execution of about INR1,300 crores is consistent with a three-month window, so there is no gap.

qa_highlights.question: How has the treasury portfolio changed, given nil other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarter-wise breakup. The other income impact comes from equity exposure marked down since 30 June; it is notional, and the company stays conservative with its investments.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a path to FY25 seamless EBITDA levels (about INR720 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the understanding is correct, provided notional inventory effects are excluded. Better margins from high-value orders and a conducive oil and gas environment were cited.

risks_watch: Notional inventory-valuation swings: margin visibility depends on steel price direction and the timing of dispatch.

Demerger into three entities: the scheme awaits exchange approval (hoped for January to February 2027); market-cap and index-flow effects on the resulting entities were raised by analysts but not addressed.
Anti-dumping duty re-imposition decision expected January 2027; import competition remains.
Other expenses are elevated versus last year, and receivables and inventory are high at 30 September; management plans to reduce both through faster execution.
Treasury exposure to equity, gold and silver ETFs drives notional other-income swings; management gave no breakup.
H2 execution of about 230,000 seamless tons depends on the Telangana finishing line commissioning in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Defensive on margins: management repeatedly called the Q2 EBITDA decline notional and reversible, and was evasive on treasury breakup, demerger rationale and the anti-dumping duty. It was more confident on order momentum, export demand and the 430,000-ton volume target.
key_quotes: It is entirely notional, and there is no impact on actual profitability of the company or the orders that it is receiving.
We will see good margins coming in the December quarter.
Regarding the 430,000 tons guidance, I think we are on track because we have done around 200,000 tons.
We reassure you that the profitability of the company is not impacted.

quality.why: The brief gives no YoY revenue growth figure and no stated growth driver for Q2; the main discussed effects are QoQ margin pressure from a notional inventory-valuation write-down and nil treasury income, which depress profit rather than explain revenue growth, while volume rose only ~7,000 t (seamless) and ~9,000 t (ERW) QoQ and volume_growth_pct is not stated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Seamless FY27 target of 430,000 t is held, requiring about 230,000 t in H2 against about 200,000 t in H1; order book rose to INR2,200 crores from INR1,700 crores with 2-4 month execution.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says the FY25 seamless EBITDA benchmark (about INR720 crores) may be approached or surpassed, but it is caveated by notional inventory effects, so a formal raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs about 230,000 t (115% of H1 pace) and depends on Telangana commissioning, while steel price swings can distort margins and anti-dumping duty decision is due January 2027.

rows.label: Order book up to INR2,200 crores
rows.why: Order book rose more than 30% from INR1,700 crores at 31 July to INR2,200 crores, with 2-4 month execution lead time supporting Q3-Q4 revenue.

rows.label: Anti-dumping duty re-imposition decision
rows.why: DGTR recommended a flat $268/ton duty and the decision is expected January 2027; import competition remains until then.

rows.label: Three-way demerger of seamless business

tone.note: Management was confident on order momentum, export demand and the 430,000-ton volume target, but defensive on the Q2 margin drop (called notional), evasive on the treasury breakup and anti-dumping duty; analysts pushed on margin visibility and the demerger rationale.
